body.statement:
In the published-class setup of the distributed-lag RIPW estimator, suppose its three stated regularity conditions hold, the unit-specific generalized propensities are known, \(G(\Pi)\succ0\), and
\[
 \mathbb E[Y_{it}(w)]=\mu_{it}+\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}\tau_{i,t,\ell}w_{t-\ell}
\]
for every \(i\), \(t\), and \(w\), with \(w_u=0\) outside \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\).  Put \(\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\tau_{i,t,\ell}\).  Then
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}-
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}
 =o_P(1).
\]
If \(\tau_{i,t,\ell}=\tau_{i,-\ell}\) for every legal \(t\), then, for each \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\),
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}_{-\ell}
 =n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\tau_{i,-\ell}+o_P(1),
\]
which is exactly the conclusion of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo's Theorem \(4.1\) under their unit-indexed known-propensity setup and Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\).
body.proof_tex:
Write \(r_i=r_i(W_i)\).  The support overlap and \(0\leq\Pi_s\leq1\) imply \(0\leq r_i\leq c_*^{-1}\).  If \(U_i\) is any scalar entry of \(r_i\), \(r_iD_{W_i}\), \(r_iD_{W_i}^{\top}JD_{W_i}\), or \(r_iD_{W_i}^{\top}JY_i\), then the bounded design, fixed \(T\), and the uniform second-moment condition give \(\sup_i\mathbb E[U_i^2]<\infty\).  By the definition of maximal correlation,
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(U_i,U_j)|
 \leq \rho_{ij}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(U_i)\operatorname{Var}(U_j)}
 \leq C\rho_{ij}
\]
for a finite constant \(C\) independent of \(i,j,n\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\left(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(U_i-\mathbb E U_i)\right)
 \leq Cn^{-2}\sum_{i,j}\rho_{ij}=O(n^{-q}).
\]
For every \(\delta>0\), applying the elementary inequality \(\mathbf 1\{|Z|>\delta\}\leq Z^2/\delta^2\) and taking expectations shows that each such sample average differs from its expectation by \(o_P(1)\).  There are only finitely many matrix entries because \(T\) and \(p\) are fixed.

Conditional assignment on the full potential-outcome schedule gives, for every supported \(s\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[r_i\mathbf 1\{W_i=s\}f(\mathscr Y_i)\right]
 =\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\Pi_s}{\pi_i(s)}pi_i(s)f(\mathscr Y_i)\right]
 =\Pi_s\mathbb E[f(\mathscr Y_i)].
\]
Taking \(f=1\) and design coordinates yields
\[
 n^{-1}\sum_i r_i=1+o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \overline D_n:=\frac{\sum_i r_iD_{W_i}}{\sum_i r_i}=M(\Pi)+o_P(1).
\]

The grand intercept and the restrictions \(\sum_i\alpha_i=0\), \(\sum_t\lambda_t=0\) parameterize all unit constants and all common time contrasts.  Eliminating them from the weighted least-squares problem first applies \(J\) within each unit and then subtracts the weighted cross-unit mean.  Thus, on the event that its normal matrix is nonsingular, the coefficient obeys
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}=\widehat G_n^{-1}\widehat g_n,
\]
where
\[
 \widehat G_n=\frac1{nT}\sum_i r_i(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n)^{\top}J(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n),
\]
\[
 \widehat g_n=\frac1{nT}\sum_i r_i(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n)^{\top}JY_i.
\]
The outcome weighted mean drops from the second normal equation because \(\sum_i r_i(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n)=0\).  This exact elimination also shows why the grand intercept cannot be omitted when both fixed-effect sums are constrained.

The preceding finite-dimensional laws of large numbers and \(\overline D_n=M+o_P(1)\) give
\[
 \widehat G_n
 =\frac1T\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}J(D_s-M)+o_P(1)
 =G(\Pi)+o_P(1).
\]
For the numerator, replacing \(\overline D_n\) by \(M\) costs \(o_P(1)\): the replacement error is the product of \(\overline D_n-M=o_P(1)\) and a weighted outcome average that is \(O_P(1)\) by the same second-moment calculation.  Conditional assignment and the calendar-varying mean model then imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1T r_i(D_{W_i}-M)^{\top}JY_i\right]
 &=\frac1T\sum_s\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}J
 \left\{\mu_i+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}e_t\tau_{i,t,\ell}(D_s)_{t,\ell}\right\}\\
 &=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{i,t,\ell}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mu_i=(\mu_{i1},\ldots,\mu_{iT})^{\top}\), and its contribution is zero because \(\sum_s\Pi_s(D_s-M)=0\).  Averaging over \(i\) and applying the variance bound yields
\[
 \widehat g_n
 =\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}+o_P(1).
\]
Since \(G(\Pi)\succ0\), its smallest eigenvalue is positive.  Entrywise convergence in the fixed dimension implies that \(\widehat G_n\) is nonsingular with probability tending to one and \(\widehat G_n^{-1}=G(\Pi)^{-1}+o_P(1)\).  Therefore
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}
 =\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}G(\Pi)^{-1}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}+o_P(1),
\]
which is the first conclusion.  Under calendar homogeneity, the normalization \(\sum_tL_{j,t,\ell}=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\) reduces its \(j\)-th coordinate to \(n^{-1}\sum_i\tau_{i,-j}+o_P(1)\), proving the second conclusion under exactly the published design layer.
body.justification: The theorem proves the tensor as the probability limit of the correctly specified published weighted regression under its actual unit-indexed conditions.
body.gap: The published paper leaves calendar-varying dynamic DATE analysis beyond scope.
body.consumer: Users can move between the design-based published estimator and the tensor without an invalid class-inclusion claim.
